question: Which option shows the correct answer when 27°C is converted to the kelvin scale?
solution:
The correct answer is __300 K****.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Kelvin scale__ is an absolute temperature scale used in science.
 
• To convert Celsius to Kelvin, use the formula K = °C + 273.15.
 
• For 27°C, the calculation is:
K = 27 + 273.15 = 300.15 K.
 
• The value can be approximated to 300 K for simplicity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Kelvin Scale:**
 
 
• It is the SI unit of temperature and starts at absolute zero.
 
• Absolute zero is the theoretical temperature where particles have minimal motion.
 
 
 
• **Celsius Scale:**
 
 
• It is a temperature scale with 0°C as the freezing point and 100°C as the boiling point of water under standard conditions.
 
• It is widely used in daily life and non-scientific applications.
 
 
 
• **Temperature Conversion:**
 
 
• The Kelvin and Celsius scales are directly related, differing only by an additive constant of 273.15.
 
• This makes conversions between them straightforward and consistent.
